clue.text: Neither brave nor bold type

definitions.meaning: in old Westerns a brave is a Native American warrior; the white settler is set against him
bold type is heavy print, so its opposite is a light, thin typeface

explanation.surface: Someone who is neither courageous nor a bold character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for a Native American warrior; 'bold type' is printing, with the answer read as a light typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: Westerns use the word for a white settler, never a warrior; read as a typeface name it suggests light print rather than heavy.

clue.text: Office confined to conflict

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut in
agon is a Greek word for a contest or conflict

explanation.surface: Office staff stuck in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: AGON, the Greek for a contest, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The US Department of Defense headquarters building is used as a name for that department.

clue.text: Maybe Neil back to get involved in this? Yes and no

definitions.text: Maybe Neil back to get involved in this? Yes and no

parts.words: Maybe Neil back to get involved in this? Yes and no
parts.note: a rugby set piece where forwards jump for the throw; a back (Neil, say) usually stays out of it, hence yes and no

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the backs are the outside players; a set piece for the forwards both does and does not involve them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby restart after the ball goes into touch, contested by forwards in a line.

clue.text: Pleasure getting near in bed

indicators.note: getting means the word for pleasure takes in the word for near

parts.note: fun means enjoyment or pleasure
to can mean close by, as in pulling a door to

explanation.surface: Enjoying oneself when someone is close in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese-style mattress laid on the floor or a frame serves as bedding.

clue.text: Foodstuff with two things of great quality

parts.note: the cream is the best part of anything
old slang 'the cheese' means the real thing, the best

explanation.surface: A foodstuff combining two top-quality items.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft spreadable dairy product made from milk and cream is food.

clue.text: Peg back soldier in difficulty

indicators.note: in shows the reversed soldier placed inside the word for a difficulty

parts.note: a spot of bother is a difficulty, as in being in a spot

indicators.note: back tells us the word for a soldier is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Pinning down a soldier who is in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a small peg or plug that stops the vent of a cask.

clue.text: Singular trousers (with flare) an object of ridicule

definitions.meaning: one leg of flared breeches, the singular of the plural trouser word
the foolish old man of commedia dell'arte and pantomime who is mocked

explanation.surface: A single pair of flared trousers making someone a laughing stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide breeches take the name in the plural; the singular is also the foolish old man laughed at in Italian comedy.

clue.text: Old footballer's shin guards

definitions.meaning: Jimmy ... was a famous English striker of the 1960s
pieces of armour protecting the lower leg

explanation.surface: A retired footballer's shin pads.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy Greaves scored for Tottenham and England; the same word names medieval armour for the lower leg.

clue.text: Thrill from getting legless

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: The buzz you get from drinking yourself senseless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legless' is British slang for very drunk, which makes the drinking picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickling, excited sensation is a thrill.

clue.text: Batting turns awfully tense with one therein

indicators.note: with here means the jumbled word also holds the cricket word for batting inside it
therein places the letter for one inside the jumbled letters
awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of tense are jumbled

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
in cricket the side batting is said to be in

explanation.surface: A nervous batsman's turns at the crease, made dreadfully tense by one score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' jumbles TENSE, 'therein' puts I inside, and 'with' adds IN inside too: N(IN)ET(I)ES. 'Batting' wants to be the definition; the definition is 'turns', right-angle turns of ninety degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-angled change of direction is a turn of ninety degrees, so such turns are called by that number.

clue.text: Abbey wanting its first inmate

indicators.note: wanting its first means the abbey's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Tintern Abbey is a ruined abbey in the Wye valley in Wales, famous from Wordsworth's poem

explanation.surface: A monastery missing its first resident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting its first' removes the T from TINTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: An intern is a person confined, as in a camp in wartime, so an inmate.

clue.text: Seed with a hard skin

parts.note: a corn is a patch of hardened skin on the foot

explanation.surface: A seed that has a tough outer coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The oak's nut is its seed.

clue.text: From a period Middle English availed, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of availed could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A Middle English text claiming it availed someone in its day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AVAILED to DIAEVAL after ME.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes things belonging to the Middle Ages, a historical period.

clue.text: Blunt confess? Want to take that in

indicators.note: to take that in means the word for want contains the phrase for confess

parts.note: dearth means want or scarcity
to own to something is to admit or confess it

explanation.surface: A frank instruction to admit something and accept it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' points back to the phrase for 'confess', OWN TO, which goes inside DEARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain-speaking, practical person is called blunt or realistic.

clue.text: Free from difficulty as a badly stocked bowls shop?

definitions.meaning: no longer in danger or trouble

definitions.text: as a badly stocked bowls shop?
definitions.meaning: the balls in lawn bowls are called woods, so a shop with none has run out of them

explanation.surface: A bowls shop with nothing on its shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: In lawn bowls, the game played on a flat green, the balls are called woods.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means past the danger, like a traveller leaving a forest; a shop short of bowls has no bowling balls in stock.

clue.text: Entertainment is a knockout — in what way?

parts.note: something that floors you knocks you down, a knockout
how asks in what way

explanation.surface: A show that stuns, and the question of how.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret performance in a nightclub is entertainment.

clue.text: One running round lake is more complacent

indicators.note: round means the word for more complacent goes around the letter for lake

parts.note: smugger means more self-satisfied
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A jogger circling a lake is getting more self-satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One running' is not a jogger but someone who runs contraband, as in gun-running.
explanation.definitionFit: To run goods is to carry them illegally, so a runner of contraband.

clue.text: Trent's aim: stop such reforms

indicators.note: reforms means the preceding letters are formed again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive s included

explanation.surface: The Council of Trent set out to halt the Reformation's new faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The Council of Trent (1545-63) was the Catholic Church's response to the Reformation; 'reforms' rearranges TRENTS AIM STOP, and the faith of the Reformers is itself what the clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catholic Counter-Reformation at Trent aimed to halt the Reformed churches' faith.

clue.text: Bank gets in its security device in form of metal

parts.note: a piggy bank, so a pig is a money box
irons are shackles or fetters that secure a prisoner

explanation.surface: A bank fitting its security device made of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude iron cast from a blast furnace is a form of the metal.

clue.text: Sign briefly in European country almost includes one

indicators.note: includes means the shortened country holds the letter for one
almost means the country's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Italy is a European country
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Signing something briefly in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ITALY to ITAL, and 'includes' puts I inside to make ITIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign with one's first letters only is to put a short signature on something.

clue.text: End of play is baffling

definitions.meaning: in cricket, play for the day ends when the umpires pull up the wooden posts
to stump someone is to baffle them

explanation.surface: The end of the game is puzzling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the close of a day's play is called by the name of the wooden posts of the wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's close of play takes this name; to perplex someone is to leave them without an answer.

clue.text: What frequently observes well-hit golf ball, a gem

definitions.text: What frequently observes well-hit golf ball
definitions.meaning: Tiger Woods, the champion golfer, keeps watching his long drives

explanation.surface: A golf watcher tracking a big drive, and a gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiger Woods is the famous American golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: The golfer's gaze follows his shots; the same name belongs to a striped golden quartz gemstone.

clue.text: Working conditions

definitions.meaning: a machine that is running is said to be in this state
in horse racing, the state of the ground is described by this word

explanation.definitionFit: A going concern is a working one; racecourse ground conditions are reported as good or soft going.

clue.text: Nerds wow Kansas

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
KS is the postal abbreviation for Kansas

explanation.surface: Nerds impressing the state of Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsessive, socially awkward enthusiasts are nerds.

clue.text: Slough is so secluded following damage

indicators.note: following places the word for secluded after the word for damage

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
shy means retiring, keeping out of the way

explanation.surface: A Berkshire town described as reclusive after being wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here a slough is a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp, so it is boggy and wet.

clue.text: Most of film about a whale shows lack of restraint

indicators.note: most of means the title loses its final letter

parts.note: Free Willy is a 1993 film about a captive orca

explanation.surface: Most of a whale movie displays wild abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the final Y of the film title.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom to choose without being constrained by fate is the absence of restraint on choice.

clue.text: What symbolises strength is turning on intelligence

indicators.note: turning means the little word is read backwards

parts.note: intelligence means information or news

explanation.surface: A symbol of strength depending on intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendons stand for muscular power, as in the phrase the sinews of war.

clue.text: Referee, maybe an artist

definitions.meaning: an official who blows for fouls
James McNeill ... was an American painter

explanation.surface: A match official who might also be a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Football officials blow a whistle; Whistler painted the famous portrait of his mother.
